messages:
Alex Chen: FYI starting POC scoping with Atlas Health (enterprise healthcare). They want SSO, on‑prem option for PHI, and clear acceptance criteria. 8 week POC, two flows: triage assistant (short prompts) + clinical note drafting (longer outputs). Need to align latency/cost/quality targets + security asks. Can folks weigh in?

Samir Patel: Qs: expected QPS and typical token lengths per request? that drives latency/cost tradeoffs. Also, do they need streaming?

Alex Chen: Baseline from them: 30 concurrent users, ~5 rps peak, avg input 80 tokens, avg output 220 tokens. Streaming for note drafting ok but not mandatory.

Maria Gomez: Proposed success criteria (suggested):
- Latency: p95 end-to-end <300ms for 256-token responses (triage), <800ms for 512-token notes (if streaming enabled tolerate chunked)
- Cost: target <$0.40 per 1k input+output tokens for POC (aim to show 30-40% savings vs their current vendor)
- Quality: >=90% pass rate on curated eval prompt set (human review), hallucination rate <1% on clinical QA set
- Reliability: 99.5% uptime during business hours, automatic fallback to small-model with graceful degradation
- Security: PHI must remain in customer VPC or on-prem; no plaintext logs stored offsite
These are starting points — open to tweaks.

Danielle H.: Important sec blockers from Atlas: SOC2 required, KMS/HSM key control, detailed audit logs for every inference request, and contract language for breach notif window. They explicitly prefer Private deployment (VPC) for PHI in production; POC can run in Dedicated with strict network isolation if they agree. Also need completed security questionnaire v2 — I can fill most but need answers on data retention and telemetry.

Priya Kapoor: Pricing notes: for an 8-week POC with Dedicated capacity we typically propose:
```
- Reserved min: 4 GPU-equivalents (burst allowed)
- POC fee: $35k reserved + $6k engineering support (on-call, integration assist)
- Optional: Private deployment add-on (customer-managed infra) starts at $15k setup
```
We can present an alternative hosted usage-based estimate if they push back. Want to confirm whether they'll sign an MSA for POC.

Alex Chen: @Priya good point — they asked for an MSA. I'll draft a statement of work.

Samir Patel: For the evals, I'll need the top 120 prompts + expected outputs from their SMEs by EOD Wednesday. I'll also spin up a lightweight loadgen plan: 5 rps steady, 30 rps spike for 10m to validate autoscale.

Maria Gomez: On model choice: recommend two variants for the POC to show cost/quality tradeoffs: high-quality 70B quantized variant for note drafting, and a 13B ultra-low-latency variant for triage. We'll provide sample prompt templates and eval harness. Example runtime config we can test:
```
model: customer-highq-70b-q8
max_tokens: 1024
batching: dynamic
kv_cache: enabled
quant_profile: q8_optimized
```
This will help measure p95 and token cost.

Danielle H.: For the security questionnaire: I need to know where logs live and retention policy. Also confirm that telemetry we collect (latency metrics, error traces) will not contain PHI. If not, we need redaction in the agent.

Priya Kapoor: Quick estimate for customer-facing deck: show two scenarios: Dedicated POC ($41k + setup) vs Hosted POC (usage-based ~ $9k–$14k depending on load). Include SLA language for p95 latency and incident response.

deploy-bot: POC runbook created: /templates/poc/enterprise-healthcare -> please attach eval prompts and security Q to the runbook. :white_check_mark:

Alex Chen: Next steps: (1) Atlas to provide SME prompt set + security questionnaire answers by Wed EOD, (2) Priya to send pricing options + MSA draft by Thu, (3) Samir + Maria to deliver loadgen and eval harness by next Mon, (4) kickoff with Atlas on Mon 2pm PT. If anyone sees major redlines, flag here. :thumbsup:

Maria Gomez: I'll prepare a short demo script focusing on hallucination checks and fallback behavior.

Samir Patel: I'll also include raw cost projection sheet (tokens and infra) to show unit economics.

Danielle H.: I'll start the security Q answers and flag any must-have contract language.

Alex Chen: Great — thanks all. I'll update the runbook with timelines and share the draft SOW shortly.
